hoa-restoration-services.name: Restoration Services for HOAs and Community Associations
hoa-restoration-services.title: HOA Restoration Services in DFW | Go Green Restoration TX
hoa-restoration-services.description: Property restoration services for DFW HOAs and condo associations. Plan water, fire, sewage cleanup and repairs with our Wylie team. Request an HOA estimate.
hoa-restoration-services.intro: A leak in a clubhouse or damage across several units can leave an HOA board with urgent decisions. Go Green Restoration TX Inc provides property restoration services for HOAs and condominium associations across Dallas, Collin County, and wider DFW from our Wylie location. Contact us about water damage, fire and smoke cleanup, sewage cleanup, repairs, or mold concerns. We’ll discuss the affected spaces, who can approve the work, and the next steps for your property.
sections: Who can authorize the work?

Start with the community address, affected buildings or units, and whether the source of damage is still active. Give us the board representative or manager’s contact details and explain who can authorize access and approve an estimate. If emergency work and later repairs need different approvals, flag that early. Also tell us whether a plumber, roofer, or other provider is already addressing the source.
Common areas and individual units

A shared hallway, a clubhouse, and the inside of an individual unit may involve different decision makers. List each affected space in the proposed scope rather than treating the whole community as a single job. The association should confirm responsibilities under its governing documents with its manager, insurer, or adviser; a restoration estimate does not decide who is responsible for a loss.
Resident access and communication

For an occupied community, the work plan needs to account for the people who live there. Discuss entry windows, keys, resident notices, parking, and equipment locations before scheduling. Choose one association contact for updates and approval of changes. Share any restrictions affecting common routes or rooms so these can be considered when planning the work area and resident communications.
From cleanup to repair

Emergency cleanup, drying, and rebuilding have different milestones. Ask which materials are being evaluated, what removal is proposed, and what must happen before repair work starts. Discuss any community requirements for finishes and replacement materials during planning. Changes to finishes or added improvements should be recorded separately from the original damage repair.
Documentation for association records

Ask what photographs, estimates, invoices, and progress records will be provided. Keep records organized by building, unit, and common area where practical. Share your insurer’s documentation requirements before work begins. The insurer determines coverage; neither a contractor estimate nor a photo guarantees payment.
What to include in your HOA estimate request

A useful first message can be short: the property location, affected rooms or common areas, when the damage appeared, and whether it is an emergency. Include the name of the person coordinating access and approvals. Existing photos or reports can help explain the situation if available. Share vendor onboarding or reporting requirements during the call so the project arrangements can be confirmed before work begins.

faqs.question: Can you discuss damage affecting both common areas and individual units?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tell us which spaces are affected and who is authorized to approve work in each. The proposed scope should identify those areas separately, including access arrangements. The association and unit owners need to confirm responsibility and insurance questions with their own advisers.

faqs.question: What affects the estimate?
faqs.answer: The affected materials, access, equipment, removal and disposal, and later repairs influence the scope. Ask for mitigation and reconstruction to be itemized separately, with a written process for approving additional work. Coverage and payment responsibilities should be confirmed with your insurer and the people authorized to approve work.

faqs.question: How quickly can you arrive?
faqs.answer: For emergencies, we aim to arrive at the property within one hour. Call to confirm current crew availability and the arrival estimate for your address. Repair schedules are separate from emergency arrival and depend on the agreed scope.

faqs.question: What mold work is available?
faqs.answer: Our current mold cleanup scope is less than 25 contiguous square feet. Larger areas and work outside that scope are referred to a TDLR-licensed remediator. A service estimate is not independent mold assessment or clearance testing.

property-management-restoration.name: Restoration Services for DFW Property Managers
property-management-restoration.title: Property Manager Restoration Services in DFW | Go Green
property-management-restoration.description: Restoration for DFW property managers: access planning, tenant coordination, documented scope, cleanup and repairs. Discuss your property with our Wylie team.
property-management-restoration.intro: A property manager needs to coordinate the owner, occupants, and the work itself. Go Green Restoration serves managed properties throughout DFW from Wylie. Tell us the property type, affected spaces, and approval requirements so we can discuss cleanup and repairs with a clear point of contact.
sections: Information for the first call

Share the property address, affected unit or common area, when the damage was noticed, and whether water or another source is still active. Identify the person authorized to approve work and the contact who can arrange access. Existing inspection findings and repair records can help explain what has already been addressed.
Tenant access and occupied spaces

Before scheduling work, agree on entry arrangements, notice requirements, access windows, and the manager’s communication process. Explain any accessibility needs or restrictions that affect the work area. Discuss equipment placement, work-area separation, and which spaces may be unavailable; occupancy decisions may require input from the relevant professionals or authorities.
Keep source repair and restoration coordinated

A plumbing or roof repair and the resulting property cleanup can require separate providers and scopes. Establish who is handling each task. Ask how moisture concerns, material removal, cleaning, drying review, and reconstruction fit together so new finishes are not scheduled before preceding work is ready.
Document changes and owner approvals

Request an itemized estimate, exclusions, and a change-approval process. Identify any spending limits or required owner approval before work begins. If additional damage is found, agree on the revised scope rather than assuming it is covered by the original authorization. Your insurer determines policy coverage.
Plan repairs and optional upgrades separately

Replacing damaged materials and changing finishes are different budget decisions. Clarify material allowances, selections, and any inspections or specialty trades involved. Procurement and approvals can affect the repair schedule, so a target emergency arrival time should not be treated as a completion promise.
Organize records for the next person

Keep estimates, approved changes, photographs, invoices, and available completion records together for the property. Discuss reporting needs during intake, including how records should identify units or common areas. For multiple properties, confirm scope and commercial terms for each request; do not assume a portfolio discount or priority dispatch arrangement.
